trial_court: District Judge, Sivasagar, Assam, Title Suit (M) No. 85/2016
case_name: Sri Rameshwar Sahu vs Smti Snehalata Chameli (Sahu)
facts_of_case: The parties got married in 1991 but had a quarrel and the wife refused to co-habit with the husband. The husband filed for divorce under Section 13(1)(i-a) and (i-b) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, which was granted by the trial court. The trial court awarded a sum of Rs. 7 lakhs as permanent alimony to the wife.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the person who is best placed to do so.
legal_principles.held: the burden is on him u/s 106 Evidence Act

legal_principles.principle: A person's current liability should be considered when determining permanent alimony.
legal_principles.held: Considering the fact that as the petitioner-husband is serving as teacher in a Government school and as there is nothing on record to show that he has any other liability except to maintain himself

legal_principles.principle: A person's ability to maintain themselves should be considered when determining permanent alimony.
legal_principles.held: I am of the opinion that if an amount of Rs. 7,00,000/- (Rupees Seven Lacs) is granted towards permanent alimony it will be just and proper for the O.P.-wife to maintain herself

outcome.final_order: The final order modified the quantum of permanent alimony from Rs. 7 lakhs to [amount not specified].

use_for_drafting: assisting in alimony and maintenance matters
